go:39529.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: GA-01
go:39529.question:
The man who is now Municipal Commissioner worked as ________________.

  1. the security guard at a university
  2. a security guard at the university
  3. a security guard at university
  4. the security guard at the university

detailed_solution.markdown: He was a security guard (one of several, not a specific one) at the university (the particular university in the context).

go:39531.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: GA-02
go:39531.question:
Nobody knows how the Indian cricket team is going to cope with the difficult and seamer-friendly wickets in Australia.

Choose the option which is closest in meaning to the underlined phrase in the above sentence.

  1. Put up with.
  2. Put in with.
  3. Put down to.
  4. Put up against.

detailed_solution.markdown: To cope with something means to manage or tolerate it, i.e. to put up with it.

go:39530.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: GA-03
go:39530.question:
Find the odd one in the following group of words.

mock, deride, praise, jeer

  1. Mock
  2. Deride
  3. Praise
  4. Jeer

detailed_solution.markdown: Mock, deride and jeer all mean to make fun of someone. Praise is the opposite.

go:39528.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: GA-04
go:39528.question:
Pick the odd one from the following options.

  1. $\text{CADBE}$
  2. $\text{JHKIL}$
  3. $\text{XVYWZ}$
  4. $\text{ONPMQ}$

detailed_solution.markdown:
Letter positions:

- CADBE = 3, 1, 4, 2, 5 (steps $-$2, +3, $-$2, +3)

- JHKIL = 10, 8, 11, 9, 12 (same steps)

- XVYWZ = 24, 22, 25, 23, 26 (same steps)

- ONPMQ = 15, 14, 16, 13, 17 (different steps)

go:39532.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: GA-05
go:39532.question:
In a quadratic function, the value of the product of the roots $(\alpha, \beta)$ is $4$. Find the value of

                        $\dfrac{\alpha^{n}+\beta^{n}}{\alpha^{-n}+\beta^{-n}}$

  1. $n^{4}$
  2. $4^{n}$
  3. $2^{2n-1}$
  4. $4^{n-1}$

detailed_solution.markdown: $\alpha^{-n}+\beta^{-n}=\frac{\alpha^n+\beta^n}{(\alpha\beta)^n}$, so the ratio is $(\alpha\beta)^n=4^n$.

go:39536.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: GA-06
go:39536.question:
Among $150$ faculty members in an institute, $55$ are connected with each other through Facebook and $85$ are connected through Whatsapp. $30$ faculty members do not have Facebook or Whatsapp accounts. The numbers of faculty members connected only through Facebook accounts is _______.

  1. $35$
  2. $45$
  3. $65$
  4. $90$

detailed_solution.markdown:
Members with at least one account = 150 $-$ 30 = 120.

Both = 55 + 85 $-$ 120 = 20.

Only Facebook = 55 $-$ 20 = 35.

go:39533.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: GA-07
go:39533.question:
Computers were invented for performing only high-end useful computations. However, it is no understatement that they have taken over our world today. The internet, for example, is ubiquitous. Many believe that the internet itself is an unintended consequence of the original invention. With the advent of mobile computing on our phones, a whole new dimension is now enabled. One is left wondering if all these developments are good or, more importantly, required.

Which of the statement(s) below is/are logically valid and can be inferred from the above paragraph?

(i) The author believes that computers are not good for us.

(ii) Mobile computers and the internet are both intended inventions.

  1. (i) only
  2. (ii) only
  3. Both (i) and (ii)
  4. Neither (i) nor (ii)

detailed_solution.markdown: Checking each statement: - (i): the author only wonders whether these developments are good or needed; he does not say computers are bad False - (ii): the passage calls the internet an unintended consequence False

go:39534.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: GA-08
go:39534.question:
All hill-stations have a lake. Ooty has two lakes.

Which of the statement(s) below is/are logically valid and can be inferred from the above sentences?

  1. Ooty is not a hill-station.
  2. No hill-station can have more than one lake.
  1. (i) only.
  2. (ii) only.
  3. Both (i) and (ii)
  4. Neither (i) nor (ii)

detailed_solution.markdown: "All hill-stations have a lake" means at least one lake; having two lakes does not contradict it. So Ooty can still be a hill-station, and hill-stations can have more than one lake.

go:39537.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: GA-09
go:39537.question:
In a $2 \times 4$ rectangle grid shown below, each cell is rectangle. How many rectangles can be observed in the grid?

$$\begin{array}{|c|c|c|c|c|}\hline{\;\;\;}&{\;\;\;}&{\;\;\;}&{\;\;\;}\\\hline{}&{}&{}&\\\hline\end{array}$$

  1. $21$
  2. $27$
  3. $30$
  4. $36$

detailed_solution.markdown:
A rectangle is fixed by choosing 2 of the 3 horizontal lines and 2 of the 5 vertical lines:

$\binom32\times\binom52=3\times10=30$

The graph is a "tent": maximum value 2 at x = 1, slope +1 on the left and $-$1 on the right (f($-$3) = $-$2, f(3) = 0).

That is $f(x)=2-|x-1|$ (check: f($-$3) = 2 $-$ 4 = $-$2, f(3) = 2 $-$ 2 = 0).

go:39568.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 01
go:39568.question:
Consider the following expressions:

  1. $false$
  2. $Q$
  3. $true$
  4. $P\vee Q$
  5. $\neg Q\vee P$

The number of expressions given above that are logically implied by $P \wedge (P \Rightarrow Q)$ is ___________.

detailed_solution.markdown:
$P\wedge(P\Rightarrow Q)$ means P is true and Q is true. Check each expression with P = Q = true:

- false False

- Q True, true True, $P\vee Q$ True, $\neg Q\vee P$ True

4 expressions are implied.

go:39571.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 02
go:39571.question: Let $f(x)$ be a polynomial and $g(x)=f'(x)$ be its derivative. If the degree of $(f(x)+f(-x))$ is $10$, then the degree of $(g(x) - g(-x))$ is __________.

detailed_solution.markdown: $f(x)+f(-x)$ keeps only the even powers of f (times 2). Its degree is 10, so f has an $x^{10}$ term (and no higher even power). $g(x)-g(-x)$ keeps only the odd powers of g = f'. Even powers of f become odd powers of g: $x^{10}\rightarrow10x^9$ is the highest. Degree = 9

go:39553.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 03
go:39553.question: The minimum number of colours that is sufficient to vertex-colour any planar graph is ________.

detailed_solution.markdown: By the four colour theorem, every planar graph can be properly coloured with 4 colours, and some (e.g. $K_4$) need all 4.

go:39545.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 04
go:39545.question:
Consider the systems, each consisting of $m$ linear equations in $n$ variables.

  1. If $m < n$, then all such systems have a solution.
  2. If $m > n$, then none of these systems has a solution.
  3. If $m = n$, then there exists a system which has a solution.

Which one of the following is CORRECT?

  1. $\text{I, II}$ and $\text{III}$ are true.
  2. Only $\text{II}$ and $\text{III}$ are true.
  3. Only $\text{III}$ is true.
  4. None of them is true.

go:39541.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 05
go:39541.question: Suppose that a shop has an equal number of LED bulbs of two different types. The probability of an LED bulb lasting more than $100$ hours given that it is of Type $1$ is $0.7$, and given that it is of Type $2$ is $0.4$. The probability that an LED bulb chosen uniformly at random lasts more than $100$ hours is _________.

detailed_solution.markdown:
Both types are equally likely (0.5 each). Total probability:

$P=0.5\times0.7+0.5\times0.4=0.35+0.2=0.55$

go:39549.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 06
go:39549.question: Suppose that the eigenvalues of matrix $A$ are $1, 2, 4$. The determinant of $\left(A^{-1}\right)^{T}$ is _________.

detailed_solution.markdown:
$\det A=1\times2\times4=8$. Transpose does not change the determinant, and $\det(A^{-1})=\frac{1}{\det A}$.

$\det(A^{-1})^T=\frac18=0.125$

go:39575.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 07
go:39575.question: Consider an eight-bit ripple-carry adder for computing the sum of $A$ and $B$, where $A$ and $B$ are integers represented in $2$'s complement form. If the decimal value of $A$ is one, the decimal value of $B$ that leads to the longest latency for the sum to stabilize is ___________

detailed_solution.markdown: The longest delay happens when a carry is generated at bit 0 and has to ripple through all 8 bits. A = 0000 0001, so B should be all 1s: 1111 1111 = $-$1.

go:39540.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 08
go:39540.question:
Let, $x_{1} ⊕ x_{2} ⊕ x_{3} ⊕ x_{4}= 0$ where $x_{1}, x_{2}, x_{3}, x_{4}$ are Boolean variables, and $⊕$ is the XOR operator.

Which one of the following must always be TRUE?

  1. $x_{1}x_{2}x_{3}x_{4} = 0$
  2. $x_{1}x_{3} + x_{2} = 0$
  3. $\bar{x}_{1} ⊕ \bar{x}_{3} = \bar{x}_{2} ⊕ \bar{x}_{4}$
  4. $x_{1} + x_{2} + x_{3} + x_{4} = 0$

detailed_solution.markdown:
$x_1\oplus x_2\oplus x_3\oplus x_4=0\Rightarrow x_1\oplus x_3=x_2\oplus x_4$.

Complementing both inputs of an XOR does not change it ($\bar a\oplus\bar b=a\oplus b$), so $\bar x_1\oplus\bar x_3=\bar x_2\oplus\bar x_4$ is always true.

The other options fail for x = 1111 (XOR = 0, but the product is 1, and so on).

go:39546.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 09
go:39546.question: Let $X$ be the number of distinct $16$-bit integers in $2's$ complement representation. Let $Y$ be the number of distinct $16$-bit integers in sign magnitude representation Then $X - Y$ is______.

detailed_solution.markdown:
Checking each statement:

- 2's complement: all $2^{16}$ bit patterns are different numbers.

- Sign-magnitude: +0 and $-$0 are both zero, so only $2^{16}-1$ distinct numbers.

X $-$ Y = 1

go:39547.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 10
go:39547.question: A processor has $40$ distinct instruction and $24$ general purpose registers. A $32$-bit instruction word has an opcode, two registers operands and an immediate operand. The number of bits available for the immediate operand field is_______.

detailed_solution.markdown:
Checking each statement:

- 40 instructions $\rightarrow$ opcode $\lceil\log_2 40\rceil=6$ bits

- 24 registers $\rightarrow$ 5 bits each, two operands = 10 bits

Immediate = 32 $-$ 6 $-$ 10 = 16 bits

go:39563.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 11
go:39563.question: Breadth First Search (BFS) is started on a binary tree beginning from the root vertex. There is a vertex $t$ at a distance four from the root. If $t$ is the $n^{\text{th}}$ vertex in this BFS traversal, then the maximum possible value of $n$ is __________

detailed_solution.markdown: BFS visits level by level. To make t as late as possible, levels 0-3 are full (1 + 2 + 4 + 8 = 15 nodes) and t is the last of the 16 nodes at level 4. n = 15 + 16 = 31

go:39565.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 12
go:39565.question:
The value printed by the following program is _______.

      void f (int * p, int m) { 
           m = m + 5; 
          *p = *p + m; 
           return; 
      }  
      void main  { 
       int i=5, j=10; 

       f (&i, j); 
       printf ("%d", i+j); 
     }

detailed_solution.concept: Programming in C - Programming In C
detailed_solution.markdown:
m is a copy of j: m = 10 + 5 = 15. *p is i: i = 5 + 15 = 20. j stays 10.

i + j = 20 + 10 = 30

go:39561.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 13
go:39561.question:
Assume that the algorithms considered here sort the input sequences in ascending order. If the input is already in the ascending order, which of the following are TRUE?

  1. Quicksort runs in $\Theta (n^2)$ time
  2. Bubblesort runs in $\Theta (n^2)$ time
  3. Mergesort runs in $\Theta (n)$ time
  4. Insertion sort runs in $\Theta (n)$ time
  1. I and II only
  2. I and III only
  3. II and IV only
  4. I and IV only

detailed_solution.markdown:
On already sorted input:

- Quicksort (first/last element as pivot) makes the most unbalanced splits $\rightarrow$ $\Theta(n^2)$ True

- Bubble sort with the "no swap" check stops after one pass $\rightarrow$ $\Theta(n)$ False

- Merge sort is always $\Theta(n\log n)$ False

- Insertion sort compares each element once $\rightarrow$ $\Theta(n)$ True

go:39570.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 14
go:39570.question:
The Floyd-Warshall algorithm for all-pair shortest paths computation is based on

  1. Greedy paradigm.
  2. Divide-and-conquer paradigm.
  3. Dynamic Programming paradigm.
  4. Neither Greedy nor Divide-and-Conquer nor Dynamic Programming paradigm.

detailed_solution.markdown: Floyd-Warshall builds $d_k[i][j]=\min(d_{k-1}[i][j],\ d_{k-1}[i][k]+d_{k-1}[k][j])$, reusing answers of smaller subproblems. That is dynamic programming.

go:39557.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 15
go:39557.question:
$N$ items are stored in a sorted doubly linked list. For a delete operation, a pointer is provided to the record to be deleted. For a decrease-key operation, a pointer is provided to the record on which the operation is to be performed.

An algorithm performs the following operations on the list in this order: $\Theta \left(N\right)$ delete, $O (\log N)$ insert, $O(\log N)$ find, and $\Theta(N)$ decrease-key. What is the time complexity of all these operations put together?

  1. $O(\log^{2} N)$
  2. $O(N)$
  3. $O(N^{2})$
  4. $\Theta\left(N^{2}\log N\right)$

detailed_solution.markdown:
In a sorted doubly linked list (pointers given for delete and decrease-key):

- delete: $O(1)$ each $\rightarrow$ $\Theta(N)$ in total

- insert: find the position, $O(N)$ each $\rightarrow$ $O(N\log N)$

- find: $O(N)$ each $\rightarrow$ $O(N\log N)$

- decrease-key: the node may have to move back towards the front, $O(N)$ each $\rightarrow$ $O(N^2)$

Total = $O(N^2)$

go:39562.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 16
go:39562.question:
The number of states in the minimum sized DFA that accepts the language defined by the regular expression.

$(0+1)^{*} (0+1) (0+1)^{*}$

is ________.

detailed_solution.markdown: $(0+1)^*(0+1)(0+1)^*=(0+1)^+$: every non-empty string. The DFA needs a non-final start state (for $\epsilon$) and one final state that loops on 0 and 1.

go:39542.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 17
go:39542.question:
Language $L_{1}$ is defined by the grammar: $S_{1} \rightarrow a S_{1} b \mid \varepsilon$

Language $L_{2}$ is defined by the grammar: $S_{2} \rightarrow a b S_{2} \mid \varepsilon$

Consider the following statements:

  • P: $L_{1}$ is regular
  • Q: $L_{2}$ is regular

Which one of the following is TRUE?

  1. Both $P$ and $Q$ are true.
  2. $P$ is true and $Q$ is false.
  3. $P$ is false and $Q$ is true.
  4. Both $P$ and $Q$ are false.

detailed_solution.markdown:
Checking each statement:

- $L_1=\{a^nb^n\}$: needs counting $\rightarrow$ not regular (P false).

- $L_2=(ab)^*$ $\rightarrow$ regular (Q true).

go:39574.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 18
go:39574.question:
Consider the following types of languages: $L_{1}$: Regular, $L_{2}$: Context-free, $L_{3}$: Recursive, $L_{4}$: Recursively enumerable. Which of the following is/are TRUE ?

  1. $\overline{L_{3}} \cup L_{4}$ is recursively enumerable.
  2. $\overline{L_{2}} \cup L_{3}$ is recursive.
  3. $L^{*} _{1} \cap L_{2}$ is context-free.
  4. $L_{1} \cup \overline{L_{2}}$ is context-free.
  1. I only.
  2. I and III only.
  3. I and IV only.
  4. I, II and III only.

detailed_solution.markdown:
Checking each statement:

- I: $\bar L_3$ is recursive (so RE), and RE is closed under union $\rightarrow$ RE True

- II: a CFL is recursive, so $\bar L_2$ is recursive; union of recursive languages is recursive True

- III: $L_1^*$ is regular (so CFL); CFL $\cup$ CFL is CFL True

- IV: $\bar L_2$ need not be CFL, so the union need not be False

go:39548.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 19
go:39548.question:
Match the following:$$\begin{array}{ll|ll}\hline \text{(P)} & \text{Lexical analysis} & \text{(i)} & \text{Leftmost derivation} \\\hline  \text{(Q)} & \text{Top down parsing} & \text{(ii)}& \text{Type checking} \\\hline   \text{(R)}& \text{Semantic analysis} & \text{(iii)}  & \text{Regular expressions} \\\hline  \text{(S)} & \text{Runtime environment} &\text{(iv)}  & \text{Activation records}  \\\hline \end{array}$$

  1. $\text{P $\leftrightarrow$ i, Q $\leftrightarrow$ ii, R $\leftrightarrow$ iv, S $\leftrightarrow$ iii}$
  2. $\text{P $\leftrightarrow$ iii, Q $\leftrightarrow$ i, R $\leftrightarrow$ ii, S $\leftrightarrow$ iv}$
  3. $\text{P $\leftrightarrow$ ii, Q $\leftrightarrow$ iii, R $\leftrightarrow$ i, S $\leftrightarrow$ iv}$
  4. $\text{P $\leftrightarrow$ iv, Q $\leftrightarrow$ i, R $\leftrightarrow$ ii, S $\leftrightarrow$ iii}$

detailed_solution.markdown:
Checking each statement:

- P. Lexical analysis $\rightarrow$ (iii) regular expressions (token patterns)

- Q. Top-down parsing $\rightarrow$ (i) leftmost derivation

- R. Semantic analysis $\rightarrow$ (ii) type checking

- S. Runtime environments $\rightarrow$ (iv) activation records

go:39559.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 20
go:39559.question:
In which one of the following page replacement algorithms it is possible for the page fault rate to increase even when the number of allocated frames increases?

  1. LRU (Least Recently Used)
  2. OPT (Optimal Page Replacement)
  3. MRU (Most Recently Used)
  4. FIFO (First In First Out)

detailed_solution.markdown: This is Belady's anomaly, which happens with FIFO. LRU, OPT and MRU are stack algorithms: with more frames the set of pages in memory only grows, so faults never increase.

go:39569.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 21
go:39569.question:
B+ Trees are considered BALANCED because.

  1. The lengths of the paths from the root to all leaf nodes are all equal.
  2. The lengths of the paths from the root to all leaf nodes differ from each other by at most $1$.
  3. The number of children of any two non-leaf sibling nodes differ by at most $1$.
  4. The number of records in any two leaf nodes differ by at most $1$.

detailed_solution.markdown: In a B+ tree all leaves are always at the same depth (splits and merges happen at the root level), so every root-to-leaf path has the same length.

go:39550.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 22
go:39550.question:
Suppose a database schedule $S$ involves transactions $T_1,\ldots,T_n$ . Construct the precedence graph of $S$  with vertices representing the transactions and edges representing the conflicts. If $S$ is serializable, which one of the following orderings of the vertices of the precedence graph is guaranteed to yield a serial schedule?

  1. Topological order
  2. Depth-first order
  3. Breadth-first order
  4. Ascending order of the transaction indices

detailed_solution.markdown: Each edge $T_i\rightarrow T_j$ means $T_i$ must come first. A serializable schedule has an acyclic precedence graph, and any topological order respects every edge, so it gives an equivalent serial schedule.

go:39555.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 23
go:39555.question:
Anarkali digitally signs a message and sends it to Salim. Verification of the signature by Salim requires.

  1. Anarkali's public key.
  2. Salim's public key.
  3. Salim's private key.
  4. Anarkali's private key.

detailed_solution.markdown: Anarkali signs with her private key, so anyone (Salim) verifies with her public key.

go:39543.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 24
go:39543.question:
In an Ethernet local area network, which one of the following statements is TRUE?

  1. A station stops to sense the channel once it starts transmitting a frame.
  2. The purpose of the jamming signal is to pad the frames that are smaller than the minimum frame size.
  3. A station continues to transmit the packet even after the collision is detected.
  4. The exponential back off mechanism reduces the probability of collision on retransmissions.

detailed_solution.markdown:
Checking each statement:

- A station keeps sensing while transmitting (that is how it detects collisions) False

- The jam signal tells everyone a collision happened; padding is something else False

- After a collision the station stops transmitting False

- Exponential backoff makes stations wait random, growing times, so they are less likely to collide again True

go:39572.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 25
go:39572.question:
Identify the correct sequence in which the following packets are transmitted on the network by a host when a browser requests a webpage from a remote server, assuming that the host has just been restarted.

  1. HTTP GET request, DNS query, TCP SYN
  2. DNS query, HTTP GET request, TCP SYN
  3. DNS query, TCP SYN, HTTP GET request.
  4. TCP SYN, DNS query, HTTP GET request.

detailed_solution.markdown: After a restart, nothing is cached: 1. DNS query to get the server's IP 2. TCP SYN to open the connection 3. HTTP GET on that connection

go:39603.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 26
go:39603.question:
A binary relation $R$ on $\mathbb{N} \times \mathbb{N}$ is defined as follows: $(a, b) R(c, d)$ if $a \leq c$ or $b \leq d$. Consider the following propositions:

  • $P:$ $R$ is reflexive.
  • $Q:$ $R$ is transitive.

Which one of the following statements is TRUE?

  1. Both $P$ and $Q$ are true.
  2. $P$ is true and $Q$ is false.
  3. $P$ is false and $Q$ is true.
  4. Both $P$ and $Q$ are false.

detailed_solution.markdown:
Checking each statement:

- Reflexive: (a, b) R (a, b) since $a\le a$ True

- Transitive fails: (3, 2) R (1, 3) because 2 $\le$ 3, and (1, 3) R (2, 1) because 1 $\le$ 2, but (3, 2) R (2, 1) needs 3 $\le$ 2 or 2 $\le$ 1 $\text{---}$ both false.

go:39618.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 27
go:39618.question:
Which one of the following well-formed formulae in predicate calculus is NOT valid ?

  1. $(\forall _{x} p(x) \implies \forall _{x} q(x)) \implies (\exists _{x} \neg p(x) \vee \forall _{x} q(x))$
  2. $(\exists x p(x) \vee \exists x q (x)) \implies \exists x (p(x) \vee q (x))$
  3. $\exists x (p(x) \wedge q(x)) \implies (\exists x p(x) \wedge \exists x q(x))$
  4. $\forall x (p(x) \vee q(x)) \implies (\forall x p(x) \vee \forall x q(x))$

detailed_solution.markdown:
Option 4 is not valid: take a domain {1, 2} with p(1), q(2) true and p(2), q(1) false. Then every x satisfies p(x) $\vee$ q(x), but neither "all p" nor "all q" holds.

Options 1-3 are standard valid implications.

go:39595.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 28
go:39595.question:
Consider a set $U$ of $23$ different compounds in a chemistry lab. There is a subset $S$ of $U$ of $9$ compounds, each of which reacts with exactly $3$ compounds of $U$. Consider the following statements:

  1. Each compound in U \ S reacts with an odd number of compounds.
  2. At least one compound in U \ S reacts with an odd number of compounds.
  3. Each compound in U \ S reacts with an even number of compounds.

Which one of the above statements is ALWAYS TRUE?

  1. Only I
  2. Only II
  3. Only III
  4. None.

detailed_solution.markdown: Model compounds as vertices and reactions as edges. The sum of all degrees is even (handshake lemma). The 9 compounds in S have degree 3 each: total 27 (odd). So the degrees of U \ S must add to an odd number, which needs at least one odd degree there. Nothing forces every one to be odd.

go:39588.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 29
go:39588.question: The value of the expression $13^{99}\pmod{17}$ in the range $0$ to $16$, is ________.

detailed_solution.markdown:
$13\equiv-4\pmod{17}$, so $13^2\equiv16\equiv-1$ and $13^4\equiv1$.

$99=4\times24+3\Rightarrow13^{99}\equiv13^3=13^2\cdot13\equiv-13\equiv4\pmod{17}$

go:39627.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 30
go:39627.question: Suppose the functions $F$ and $G$ can be computed in $5$ and $3$ nanoseconds by functional units $U_{F}$ and $U_{G}$, respectively. Given two instances of $U_{F}$ and two instances of $U_{G}$, it is required to implement the computation $F(G(X_{i}))$ for $1 \leq i \leq 10$. Ignoring all other delays, the minimum time required to complete this computation is ____________ nanoseconds.

detailed_solution.markdown:
Each item needs G (3 ns) then F (5 ns). With 2 units of each, the F units are the bottleneck: 10 F computations on 2 units = 5 rounds $\times$ 5 ns = 25 ns.

F can start only after the first G results are ready (3 ns), and the G units keep feeding F in time after that.

Total = 3 + 25 = 28 ns

go:39601.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 31
go:39601.question: Consider a processor with $64$ registers and an instruction set of size twelve. Each instruction has five distinct fields, namely, opcode, two source register identifiers, one destination register identifier, and twelve-bit immediate value. Each instruction must be stored in memory in a byte-aligned fashion. If a program has $100$ instructions, the amount of memory (in bytes) consumed by the program text is _________.

detailed_solution.markdown:
Checking each statement:

- Opcode: 12 instructions $\rightarrow$ 4 bits

- 3 register fields: 64 registers $\rightarrow$ 6 bits each = 18 bits

- Immediate: 12 bits

Total = 34 bits $\rightarrow$ byte-aligned = 5 bytes per instruction. 100 instructions $\times$ 5 = 500 bytes.

go:39622.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 32
go:39622.question: The width of the physical address on a machine is $40$ bits. The width of the tag field in a $512$ KB $8$-way set associative cache is ________ bits.

detailed_solution.markdown:
One way = 512 KB / 8 = 64 KB = $2^{16}$ bytes, so index + offset = 16 bits.

Tag = 40 $-$ 16 = 24 bits

go:39580.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 33
go:39580.question: Consider a $3 \ \text{GHz}$ (gigahertz) processor with a three stage pipeline and stage latencies $\large\tau_1,\tau_2$ and $\large\tau_3$ such that $\large\tau_1 =\dfrac{3 \tau_2}{4}=2\tau_3$. If the longest pipeline stage is split into two pipeline stages of equal latency , the new frequency is __________ $\text{GHz}$, ignoring delays in the pipeline registers.

detailed_solution.markdown:
Let $\tau_1=6k$: then $\tau_2=8k$ and $\tau_3=3k$. The clock is set by the longest stage, 8k, at 3 GHz.

Split $\tau_2$ into two stages of 4k. Now the longest is $\tau_1=6k$.

New frequency $=3\times\frac{8k}{6k}=4$ GHz

go:39585.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 34
go:39585.question: A complete binary min-heap is made by including each integer in $[1, 1023]$ exactly once. The depth of a node in the heap is the length of the path from the root of the heap to that node. Thus, the root is at depth $0$. The maximum depth at which integer $9$ can appear is _________.

detailed_solution.markdown: In a min-heap every ancestor of 9 must be smaller than 9. Only 1-8 are smaller, so 9 can have at most 8 ancestors $\rightarrow$ depth at most 8. This is possible: put 1, 2, $\ldots$, 8, 9 down one path (the heap of 1023 nodes has depths 0-9).

go:39578.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 35
go:39578.question:
The following function computes $X^{Y}$ for positive integers $X$ and $Y$.

int exp (int X, int Y) { 
     int res =1, a = X, b = Y;
   
     while (b != 0) { 
         if (b % 2 == 0) {a = a * a; b = b/2; } 
         else         {res = res * a; b = b - 1; } 
     } 
     return res; 
}

Which one of the following conditions is TRUE before every iteration of the loop?

  1. $X^{Y} = a^{b}$
  2. $(res * a)^{Y} = (res * X)^{b}$
  3. $X^{Y} = res * a^{b}$
  4. $X^{Y} = (res * a)^{b}$

detailed_solution.markdown:
Check that $res\cdot a^b$ stays equal to $X^Y$:

- Start: $1\cdot X^Y$ True

- b even: $a\rightarrow a^2,\ b\rightarrow b/2$, and $(a^2)^{b/2}=a^b$ True

- b odd: $res\rightarrow res\cdot a,\ b\rightarrow b-1$, and $(res\cdot a)a^{b-1}=res\cdot a^b$ True

When b = 0, res = $X^Y$.

go:39597.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 36
go:39597.question:
Consider the following New-order strategy for traversing a binary tree:

  • Visit the root;
  • Visit the right subtree using New-order;
  • Visit the left subtree using New-order;

The New-order traversal of the expression tree corresponding to the reverse polish expression

3 4 * 5 - 2 ^ 6 7 * 1 + -

is given by:

  1. $+ -  1 \ 6 \ 7 * 2 \wedge 5 \ - \ 3 \ 4 \ *$
  2. $- +  1 *  6 \ 7 \wedge 2 - 5 * 3 \ 4$ 
  3. $- +  1 * 7 \ 6  \wedge 2 \ - \ 5 \ * \ 4 \ 3 $
  4. $1 \ 7 \ 6 *  + \ 2 \ 5  \ 4 \ 3 \ * \ - \wedge -$

detailed_solution.markdown:
Expression tree of 3 4 * 5 - 2 ^ 6 7 * 1 + - :

root $-$, left = ((3*4) $-$ 5) ^ 2, right = (6*7) + 1.

New-order = root, right subtree, left subtree:

- root: $-$

- right: + 1 * 7 6

- left: ^ 2 $-$ 5 * 4 3

go:39602.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 37
go:39602.question:
Consider the following program:

int f (int * p, int n) 
{ 
    if (n <= 1) return 0; 
    else return max (f (p+1, n-1), p[0] - p[1]); 
}
 int main  
{
    int a = {3, 5, 2, 6, 4}; 
    printf(" %d", f(a, 5)); 
}

Note: $\max (x, y)$ returns the maximum of $x$ and $y$.

The value printed by this program is ________.

detailed_solution.concept: Programming in C - Programming In C
detailed_solution.markdown:
f returns the largest value of p[i] $-$ p[i+1] over neighbouring pairs (or 0):

3 $-$ 5 = $-$2, 5 $-$ 2 = 3, 2 $-$ 6 = $-$4, 6 $-$ 4 = 2

max = 3

go:39587.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 38
go:39587.question: Let $A_{1}, A_{2}, A_{3}$ and $A_{4}$ be four matrices of dimensions $10 \times 5, 5 \times 20, 20 \times 10$ and $10 \times 5$, respectively. The minimum number of scalar multiplications required to find the product $A_{1}A_{2}A_{3}A_{4}$ using the basic matrix multiplication method is _________.

detailed_solution.markdown: Dimensions 10, 5, 20, 10, 5. Matrix chain DP: - Pairs: A1A2 = 1000, A2A3 = 1000, A3A4 = 1000 - A2A3A4: (A2A3)A4 = 1000 + 5$\cdot$10$\cdot$5 = 1250 - A1A2A3A4: A1((A2A3)A4) = 1250 + 10$\cdot$5$\cdot$5 = 1500 (other splits give 3000 and 2000)

go:39581.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 39
go:39581.question:
The given diagram shows the flowchart for a recursive function $A(n)$. Assume that all statements, except for the recursive calls, have $O(1)$ time complexity. If the worst case time complexity of this function is $O(n^{\alpha})$, then the least possible value (accurate up to two decimal positions) of $\alpha$ is ________.

Flow chart for Recursive Function $A(n)$.

detailed_solution.markdown: Worst-case path in the flowchart: A(n/2) at the start, then the right branch with two calls, then down with one more call, then the left branch with one more call. That is 5 calls to A(n/2). $T(n)=5T(n/2)+O(1)\Rightarrow T(n)=O(n^{\log_2 5})=O(n^{2.32})$

go:39586.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 40
go:39586.question:
The number of ways in which the numbers $1, 2, 3, 4, 5, 6, 7$ can be inserted in an empty binary search tree, such that the resulting tree has height $6$, is _________.

Note: The height of a tree with a single node is $0$.

detailed_solution.markdown:
Height 6 with 7 nodes means the tree is a single path. After each insertion, the next number must be the smallest or the largest of the numbers still left (2 choices each), and the last number is forced.

$2^6=64$

go:39620.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 41
go:39620.question:
In an adjacency list representation of an undirected simple graph $G=(V, E)$, each edge $(u, v)$ has two adjacency list entries: $[v]$ in the adjacency list of $u$, and $[u]$ in the adjacency list of $v$. These are called twins of each other. A twin pointer is a pointer from an adjacency list entry to its twin. If $|E|=m$ and $|V|=n$, and the memory size is not a constraint, what is the time complexity of the most efficient algorithm to set the twin pointer in each entry in each adjacency list?

  1. $\Theta\left(n^{2}\right)$
  2. $\Theta\left(n+m\right)$
  3. $\Theta\left(m^{2}\right)$
  4. $\Theta\left(n^{4}\right)$

detailed_solution.markdown: Go through all edges once (scanning every adjacency list), using an n $\times$ n table (memory is no problem) to remember where entry [v] in u's list is. When you meet [u] in v's list, look up its twin and link them. Each of the 2m entries is handled once, plus $O(n)$ to scan the lists.

go:39591.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 42
go:39591.question:
Consider the following two statements:

  1. If all states of an NFA are accepting states then the language accepted by the NFA is $\Sigma_{}^{*}$.
  2. There exists a regular language $A$ such that for all languages $B$, $A \cap B$ is regular.

Which one of the following is CORRECT?

  1. Only I is true
  2. Only II is true
  3. Both I and II are true
  4. Both I and II are false

detailed_solution.markdown:
Checking each statement:

- I: an NFA may simply have no transition for some symbol, so some strings have no path and are rejected even if every state is accepting $\text{---}$ FALSE.

- II: take $A=\phi$: $A\cap B=\phi$ is regular for every B $\text{---}$ TRUE.

go:39605.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 43
go:39605.question:
Consider the following languages:

$L_{1}=\left\{a^{n}b^{m}c^{n+m}:m, n\geq 1\right\}$

$L_{2}=\left\{a^{n}b^{n}c^{2n} :n\geq 1\right\}$

Which one of the following is TRUE?

  1. Both $L_{1}$ and $L_{2}$ are context-free.
  2. $L_{1}$ is context-free while $L_{2}$ is not context-free.
  3. $L_{2}$ is context-free while $L_{1}$ is not context-free.
  4. Neither $L_{1}$ nor $L_{2}$ is context-free.

detailed_solution.concept: Theory of Computation - Context Free Language
detailed_solution.markdown: Checking each statement: - $L_1=a^nb^mc^{n+m}$: push for every a and b, pop one per c $\rightarrow$ context-free. - $L_2=a^nb^nc^{2n}$: needs to match a with b and with c $\rightarrow$ not context-free.

go:39596.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 44
go:39596.question:
Consider the following languages.

  • $L_{1} = \left\{\left\langle M \right\rangle \mid M \text{ takes at least 2016 steps on some input} \right\}$,
  • $L_{2} = \left\{\left\langle M \right\rangle \mid M \text { takes at least 2016 steps on all inputs} \right\}$ and
  • $L_{3} = \left\{\left\langle M \right\rangle \mid M \ \text {accepts }\epsilon\right\}$,

where for each Turing machine $M, \left\langle M \right\rangle$ denotes a specific encoding of $M$. Which one of the following is TRUE?

  1. $L_{1}$ is recursive and $L_{2}, L_{3}$ are not recursive
  2. $L_{2}$ is recursive and $L_{1}, L_{3}$ are not recursive
  3. $L_{1}, L_{2}$ are recursive and $L_{3}$ is not recursive
  4. $L_{1}, L_{2}, L_{3}$ are recursive

detailed_solution.concept: Theory of Computation - Recursive and Recursively Enumerable Languages
detailed_solution.markdown:
In 2016 steps a TM reads at most the first 2016 input symbols, so only inputs of length up to 2016 matter. Simulating M on all of them for 2016 steps decides both L1 and L2 $\rightarrow$ recursive.

L3 (M accepts $\varepsilon$) is a non-trivial property of L(M) $\rightarrow$ undecidable (Rice).

go:39594.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 45
go:39594.question:
Which one of the following grammars is free from left recursion?

  1. $S \rightarrow AB$
    $A \rightarrow Aa \mid b$
    $B \rightarrow c$
  2. $S \rightarrow Ab \mid Bb \mid c$
    $A \rightarrow Bd \mid \epsilon$
    $B \rightarrow e$
  3. $S \rightarrow Aa \mid B$
    $A \rightarrow Bb \mid Sc \mid \epsilon$
    $ B \rightarrow d$
  4. $S \rightarrow Aa \mid Bb \mid c$
    $A \rightarrow Bd \mid \epsilon$
    $B \rightarrow Ae \mid \epsilon$

detailed_solution.markdown: Checking each statement: - Option 1: $A\rightarrow Aa$ is directly left recursive. - Option 2: S, A, B never start with themselves, directly or indirectly True - Option 3: $S\rightarrow Aa$ and $A\rightarrow Sc$ give $S\Rightarrow Sca$ (indirect). - Option 4: $A\rightarrow Bd$ and $B\rightarrow Ae$ give $A\Rightarrow Aed$ (indirect).

go:39598.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 46
go:39598.question:
A student wrote two context-free grammars G1 and G2 for generating a single C-like array declaration. The dimension of the array is at least one. For example,

                int a[10] [3];

The grammars use D as the start symbol, and use six terminal symbols int ; id [ ] num.
$$\begin{array}{l|l} \text{Grammar } \textbf{G1}  & \text{Grammar } \textbf{G2} \\\hline \text{D} \rightarrow  \textbf{int L;} & \text{D} \rightarrow  \textbf{int L;}\\ 
\text{L} \rightarrow  \textbf{id [E} & \text{L} \rightarrow \textbf{id E}\\ \text{E} \rightarrow \textbf{num ]} & \text{E} \rightarrow \textbf{E [num]}\\ 
\text{E} \rightarrow \textbf{num ] [E} & \text{E} \rightarrow \textbf{[num]}\\ \end{array}$$Which of the grammars correctly generate the declaration mentioned above?

  1. Both G1 and G2
  2. Only G1
  3. Only G2
  4. Neither G1 nor G2

detailed_solution.markdown: Derive int a[10][3]; with each grammar: - G1: D $\rightarrow$ int L; $\rightarrow$ int id [ E ; $\rightarrow$ int id [ num ] [ E ; $\rightarrow$ int id [num] [num] ; True - G2: D $\rightarrow$ int L; $\rightarrow$ int id E ; $\rightarrow$ int id E [num] ; $\rightarrow$ int id [num] [num] ; True Both also give one or more dimensions in general.

go:39625.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 47
go:39625.question: Consider the following processes, with the arrival time and the length of the CPU burst given in milliseconds. The scheduling algorithm used is preemptive shortest remaining-time first.$$\small \begin{array}{|c|c|c|} \hline \textbf{Process} & \textbf{Arrival Time} & \textbf{Burst Time}\\\hline \text{$P_1$} & 0 & 10 \\\hline \text{$P_2$} & 3 & 6 \\\hline \text{$P_3$} & 7 & 1 \\\hline \text{$P_4$} & 8 & 3 \\\hline  \end{array}$$The average turn around time of these processes is ___________ milliseconds.

detailed_solution.markdown:
SRTF: P1 0-3 (7 left); P2 arrives (6 $\lt$ 7) and runs 3-7 (2 left); P3 (1) runs 7-8; P2 runs 8-10; P4 runs 10-13; P1 runs 13-20.

Turnaround: P1 20, P2 10 $-$ 3 = 7, P3 8 $-$ 7 = 1, P4 13 $-$ 8 = 5.

Average = 33 / 4 = 8.25

go:39600.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 48
go:39600.question:
Consider the following two-process synchronization solution.
$$\begin{array}{l|l}\hline \text{PROCESS 0 }  &  \text{Process 1 }\\  \\  \text{Entry: loop while (turn == 1); } & \text{Entry: loop while (turn == 0);} \\  \quad\text{(critical section)} &\quad \text{    (critical section)} \\ \text{Exit: turn = 1;} & \text{Exit turn = 0; }\\ \\\hline \end{array}$$

The shared variable turn is initialized to zero. Which one of the following is TRUE?

  1. This is a correct two- process synchronization solution. 
  2. This solution violates mutual exclusion requirement.
  3. This solution violates progress requirement.
  4. This solution violates bounded wait requirement.

detailed_solution.markdown: This is strict alternation: the processes must take turns. Mutual exclusion holds, but if process 0 wants to enter twice while process 1 does not want to enter at all, process 0 is blocked (turn = 1) by a process that is not even trying. That violates progress.

go:39576.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 49
go:39576.question: Consider a non-negative counting semaphore $S$. The operation $P(S)$ decrements $S$, and $V(S)$ increments $S$. During an execution, $20$ $P(S)$ operations and $12$ $V(S)$ operations are issued in some order. The largest initial value of $S$ for which at least one $P(S)$ operation will remain blocked is _______

detailed_solution.markdown: With initial value x, the 12 V operations can supply at most 12 more units, so at most x + 12 P operations can succeed. For at least one of the 20 P operations to stay blocked: $x+12 \lt 20\Rightarrow x\le7$.

go:39592.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 50
go:39592.question:
A file system uses an in-memory cache to cache disk blocks. The miss rate of the cache is shown in the figure. The latency to read a block from the cache is $1$ ms and to read a block from the disk is $10$ ms. Assume that the cost of checking whether a block exists in the cache is negligible. Available cache sizes are in multiples of $10$ MB.

The smallest cache size required to ensure an average read latency of less than $6$ ms is _________ MB.

detailed_solution.markdown: Average latency = (1 $-$ m) $\times$ 1 + m $\times$ 10 = 1 + 9m (m = miss rate). We need $1+9m \lt 6\Rightarrow m \lt 0.556$. From the graph: 20 MB gives 60% (too high), 30 MB gives 40% $\rightarrow$ latency 1 + 3.6 = 4.6 ms True

go:39590.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 51
go:39590.question:
Consider the following database schedule with two transactions $T_{1}$ and $T_{2}$.

$S= r_{2}\left(X\right); r_{1}\left(X\right); r_{2} \left(Y\right); w_{1} \left(X\right); r_{1} \left(Y\right); w_{2} \left(X\right); a_{1}; a_{2}$

Where $r_{i} (Z)$ denotes a read operation by transaction $T_{i}$ on a variable $Z$, $w_{i}(Z)$ denotes a write operation by $T_{i}$ on a variable $Z$ and $a_{i}$ denotes an abort by transaction $T_{i}$.

Which one of the following statements about the above schedule is TRUE?

  1. $S$ is non-recoverable.
  2. $S$ is recoverable, but has a cascading abort.
  3. $S$ does not have a cascading abort.
  4. $S$ is strict.

detailed_solution.markdown: No transaction reads a value written by the other before it ends: T1 reads X before T2 writes it, and T2's reads happen before T1's write. So when T1 aborts, T2 does not need to be aborted: no cascading abort. It is not strict, because $w_2(X)$ overwrites $w_1(X)$ while T1 is still active.

go:39604.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 52
go:39604.question:
Consider the following database table named water_schemes:
$$\overset{\text{Water_schemes}}{\begin{array}{|c|c|c|}\hline
\textbf{scheme_no}&    \textbf{district_name}&  \textbf{capacity} \\\hline
1&     \text{Ajmer}&       20  \\ \hline   
1&     \text{Bikaner}& 10 \\     \hline
2&     \text{Bikaner}&  10      \\\hline
3&     \text{Bikaner}&20     \\\hline
1&     \text{Churu}&     10  \\\hline    
2&     \text{Churu}& 20   \\\hline   
1&     \text{Dungargarh}&  10      \\\hline 
\end{array}}$$

The number of tuples returned by the following SQL query is _________.

with total (name, capacity) as 
    select district_name, sum (capacity) 
    from water_schemes
    group by district_name 
with total_avg (capacity) as 
   select avg (capacity) 
   from total 
select name 
   from total, total_avg 
   where total.capacity ≥ total_avg.capacity

detailed_solution.markdown:
District totals: Ajmer 20, Bikaner 10 + 10 + 20 = 40, Churu 10 + 20 = 30, Dungargarh 10.

Average of totals = (20 + 40 + 30 + 10) / 4 = 25.

Districts with total $\ge$ 25: Bikaner and Churu $\rightarrow$ 2 rows.

go:39589.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 53
go:39589.question: A network has a data transmission bandwidth of $20 \times 10^{6}$ bits per second. It uses CSMA/CD in the MAC layer. The maximum signal propagation time from one node to another node is $40$ microseconds. The minimum size of a frame in the network is __________ bytes.

detailed_solution.markdown:
For CSMA/CD the frame must still be sending when news of a collision returns: $T_t\ge2T_p$.

Min frame = $2\times40\times10^{-6}\times20\times10^6=1600$ bits = 200 bytes

go:39593.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 54
go:39593.question:
For the $\text{IEEE 802.11 MAC}$ protocol for wireless communication, which of the following statements is/are TRUE?

  1. At least three non-overlapping channels are available for transmissions.
  2. The RTS-CTS mechanism is used for collision detection.
  3. Unicast frames are ACKed.

 

  1. All I, II, and III
  2. I and III only
  3. II and III only
  4. II only

detailed_solution.markdown: Checking each statement: - I: 802.11 (2.4 GHz) has 3 non-overlapping channels (1, 6, 11) True - II: RTS/CTS is for collision avoidance (hidden terminals); wireless stations cannot detect collisions False - III: unicast frames are acknowledged True

go:39577.title: GATE CSE 2016 Set 2 | Question: 55
go:39577.question: Consider a $128 \times 10^3$ bits/second satellite communication link with one way propagation delay of $150$ milliseconds. Selective retransmission (repeat) protocol is used on this link to send data with a frame size of $1$ kilobyte. Neglect the transmission time of acknowledgement. The minimum number of bits required for the sequence number field to achieve $100 \%$ utilization is ________.

detailed_solution.markdown:
Frame = 1 KB = 8192 bits $\rightarrow$ $T_t=\frac{8192}{128000}=64$ ms. RTT = 300 ms.

For 100% utilization the window must cover $\frac{64+300}{64}\approx5.7$ $\rightarrow$ 6 frames.

Selective repeat needs window $\le2^{k-1}$: $2^{k-1}\ge6\Rightarrow k=4$.
